video_title: Wrapping the Wolves | The Jon Krawczynski Show

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves' current state and need for change
quotes.excerpt: This Timberwolves team probably went as far as it was going to go and now needs some changes.
quotes.quote: Yeah, I mean I do think it's sort of two fold right now. One is I think that in the immediate aftermath of any season ending before that you before you want it to certainly when you end with a 30-point loss at home in the in the game six. It's very easy to say everything is bad, everything needs to be changed. This is a failure. And when I think back on this season, I think it was it fell short of expectations, but I still think it was largely an enjoyable season and especially an enjoyable playoffs to see them beat Denver in six games when they're so short-handed to really take a great San Antonio team to six games when they were short-handed and so I I like I liked the way that it ended over the last couple of weeks before the game six lost to San Antonio. That said the overwhelming feeling to me right now is they're just not good enough. When you look at what San Antonio and Oklahoma City have built and the staying power that they are expected to have over the next several years that this Timberwolves team probably went as far as it was going to go and now needs some changes to close the gap on what San Antonio and Oklahoma City have become. And it is a big challenge and it is an obvious challenge because the simple fact is what Rudy Gobert said, the better team won and San Antonio was better, you know, by a significant margin.

quotes.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
quotes.summary_phrase: Timberwolves' trade and internal development options
quotes.excerpt: You make a big swing for a Giannis for a Kyrie or you make a different kind of lesser impact move.

text_blocks.speaker: Jim Souhan
text_blocks.text: Is that a Giannis trade? If it's not a Giannis trade, is there another star you could possibly get and if you can't get a star, how do you improve?

text_blocks.speaker: Jon Krawczynski
text_blocks.text: Yeah, it's so it's a couple of things. It's possibly a Giannis trade. I think it would be very hard to pull off because there will be other teams that get involved in this bidding that probably have a few more draft picks that maybe have a young player that is a little more attractive to the Bucks. Getting Giannis to pair with Anthony Edwards would be I think a significant upgrade. If you cannot pull off a Giannis deal, there are other options out there. Maybe it's Kyrie Irving. I don't know that John Morant is the dice you want to roll, but the other avenue that you can explore is if you do move like a Julius Randle or Rudy Gobert or something like that, sort of reconfiguring the hierarchy of this team. Maybe then you make Jaden McDaniels your number two. If he is a little more empowered offensively, maybe you get a little more consistency from him that way. Jaden has improved every summer for the last five years and if he were to come into this next season knowing that it's going to be Ant at the number one spot and Jaden at the number two spot, maybe you can get him to take one more leap. That kind of changes the way that everything looks and significantly bolsters their chances of being a team that can be more difficult to deal with offensively than they have been. You make a big swing for a Giannis for a Kyrie or you make a different kind of lesser impact move where you're not getting as much back in return, but you are clearing a path to see if Jaden McDaniels is ready to really be a bonafide number two scorer, two-way player all of those things.
